task.title: Fix relay mailbox immutability, envelope expiry, request bounds and identity-scoped mailbox authorization
task.description: Turn the RED tests from dispatch 001-T34-tests GREEN by implementing the four confirmed T28 review findings F-004, F-005, F-006 and F-007 in apps/relay. The tests are the contract: make them pass without weakening them.
task.scope: apps/relay production code. Do not modify apps/cli or packages/**.

acceptance_criteria: F-004 (blocker): the mailbox writer reads the existing record inside the same transaction. A byte-identical envelope replay succeeds idempotently; a changed body under an already-used (recipient mailbox, envelope_id) pair returns a conflict mapped to HTTP 409 with code ENVELOPE_ID_CONFLICT (the code apps/cli/src/transport/relayClient.ts already expects) and never replaces the stored envelope. Transaction conflicts are retried safely.

F-005 (major): already-expired envelopes are rejected at submission; physical retention never exceeds the envelope's remaining declared lifetime, and never exceeds the configured server cap either; GetEnvelopes filters expired records BEFORE applying the batch limit; an identical retry does not extend expiry.

F-006 (blocker): every v1 JSON decoder site listed in the finding bounds the request body with http.MaxBytesReader before decoding and answers with a bounded error; ValidateMailboxEnvelope verifies the ACTUAL decoded ciphertext byte length against both the declared size_bytes and the configured maximum. Other variable-length request fields/arrays are bounded as part of the same decoder contract.

F-007 (blocker): mailbox device authorization resolves the device by an immutable (mailbox identity, device UUID) binding populated by both v1 and v2 publication, never by a global first-UUID-match scan followed by an ownership comparison. A device UUID registered under an unrelated identity cannot deny service to the legitimate recipient on challenge, poll or ack.

Every test added by 001-T34-tests passes, unmodified: mailbox_envelope_lifecycle_test.go, mailbox_device_authorization_test.go, request_body_limit_test.go, mailbox_repo_test.go, mailbox_envelope_size_test.go.
`go -C apps/relay test -race -count=1 ./...` and the `-tags relayv2` variant both pass, with no pre-existing test weakened, skipped or deleted.
Existing v1 route behaviour outside these four findings is unchanged.

Implementer note from the test author (1): the F-005 retrieval test seeds Badger directly under the current key layout mailbox:<mailbox>:<envelope_id>; if you change that layout, update seedStoredEnvelope/mailboxEnvelopeKeyForTest accordingly - that is the one permitted kind of test edit, and it must be reported.

Implementer note (2): the F-006(b) test pins the current two-arg ValidateMailboxEnvelope(envelope, maxBytes) signature and reads 'actual decoded ciphertext byte length' as the JSON-decoded string length, matching the CLI contract size_bytes = Buffer.byteLength(ciphertext). Put the expiry check in the handler, not in that signature.

Implementer note (3): F-006(a) asserts boundedness, not an exact limit. The /v1/messages/send body limit must stay ABOVE MaxMessageBytes (262144); the v2 sibling's 64 KiB limit is too small for that route.
Implementer note (4): for F-005(a) prefer the INVALID_SCHEMA rejection code, since packages/** is owned by a parallel worker and carries no expiry code.
